name: APT20
affiliation_detail:
Fox-IT (2019) stated: "Fox-IT assesses with high confidence that the actor is a Chinese group and that they are likely working to support the interests of the Chinese government and are tasked with obtaining information for espionage purposes." Fox-IT's evidence for Chinese origin included: browser language settings set to Chinese, a rented server registration using a non-existent US address but with the state name "Louisiana" written in Chinese characters, and code sourced from Chinese-language forums. 
No DOJ indictment, no specific government unit, and no named individuals have been publicly identified.
description:
APT20 is a suspected Chinese state-associated cyber espionage group active since at least 2009.
In its earlier phase (2008-2014), tracked as "th3bug" by Palo Alto, the group favored watering hole attacks using Poison Ivy RAT, targeting higher education, healthcare, telecommunications, and Uyghur ethnic minority communities. After a period of apparent dormancy (2016-2017), the group re- emerged with evolved tradecraft documented by Fox-IT in "Operation Wocao" (December 2019), shifting to living-off-the-land techniques, exploiting vulnerable JBoss web servers for initial access, deploying web shells, and using legitimate system tools for lateral movement. 
The group targeted government entities, managed service providers, and organizations across aviation, construction, energy, finance, healthcare, insurance, gambling, offshore engineering, software development, and transportation in 10+ countries. 
The "Wocao" name (我操, Chinese slang for "shit" or "damn") originated from a frustrated command the hackers typed when they discovered their web shells had been removed by defenders during incident response.

campaigns.name: TH3Bug Watering Hole Campaigns
campaigns.description: APT20/th3bug conducted a series of watering hole attacks over several years, compromising legitimate websites to infect visitors with Poison Ivy RAT variants. FireEye's 2013 Poison Ivy report identified th3bug as a distinct campaign active since at least 2008. In summer 2014, Palo Alto documented the group compromising a Uyghur-language community website and other sites, such as telecom providers or US-based IT companies. The malware used Poison Ivy with the distinctive password "th3bug." Metasploit Meterpreter shells were used as intermediate downloaders. FireEye also noted in 2013 that th3bug received the IE CVE-2013-3893 exploit (originally used by APT17/ DeputyDog) shortly after it became publicly available, indicating exploit-sharing relationships in the Chinese APT ecosystem.

campaigns.name: Operation Wocao
campaigns.description: Fox-IT discovered operations with medium confidence attributed to APT20 in summer 2018 during incident response for a compromised client, ultimately documenting nearly two years of activity. The group abandoned custom malware in favor of living-off-the-land techniques. Initial access was primarily through exploitation of vulnerable JBoss enterprise application servers. APT20 leveraged web shells planted by other threat actors on already-compromised servers for reconnaissance before deploying their own access. Post-compromise, the group used legitimate tools (PowerShell, Mimikatz, ProcDump, PsExec, SMBExec, BloodHound/SharpHound, KeeThief, Kerberoast) for lateral movement, credential dumping, and Active Directory reconnaissance. A primary objective was VPN credential theft for persistent, encrypted access to victim networks. Most significantly, Fox-IT documented APT20 bypassing two-factor authentication by stealing RSA SecurID software tokens from compromised systems and generating valid one-time codes on attacker-controlled computers — effectively defeating 2FA-protected VPN access. The investigation identified victims in 10+ countries across government entities, managed service providers, and numerous industries. The campaign name originated when defenders removed APT20's web shells and the frustrated hackers typed "wocao" (我操, Chinese slang for "shit/damn") upon discovering their access was revoked.
